glossary.definition: The ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, during which Muslims observe fasting from dawn to sunset as one of the Five Pillars of Islam.
The pre-dawn meal eaten before beginning the daily fast. It's recommended to eat suhoor as close to dawn as possible for maximum energy during fasting hours.
The evening meal that breaks the daily fast at sunset. Traditionally begins with dates and water, following the Prophet's practice.
The dawn prayer and also the time when fasting begins each day. The call to Fajr prayer signals the start of the fasting period.
The sunset prayer and the time when fasting ends each day. The call to Maghrib prayer signals it's time for iftar.
Special evening prayers performed during Ramadan after the Isha (night) prayer. These prayers involve recitation of the Quran.
Obligatory charitable giving, one of the Five Pillars of Islam. During Ramadan, many Muslims calculate and pay their annual zakat.
Voluntary charitable giving beyond zakat. The rewards for sadaqah are believed to be multiplied during Ramadan.
The Arabic word for fasting. Sawm is one of the Five Pillars of Islam and involves abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs from dawn to sunset.
The Night of Power or Decree, believed to fall within the last ten nights of Ramadan. It commemorates the night the Quran was first revealed.
The Festival of Breaking Fast, a three-day celebration marking the end of Ramadan. It begins with a special prayer and involves family gatherings, gift-giving, and festive meals.
The holy book of Islam, believed to be the word of God revealed to Prophet Muhammad. Ramadan is the month when its revelation began.
Personal supplication or prayer to God. The moment just before breaking fast is considered an especially blessed time for dua.
Intention. Making the intention to fast is an essential part of the fasting practice, typically made before Fajr.

Charity due at the end of Ramadan, distinct from fitrah (innate disposition). Sahih al-Bukhari 1503 describes a sa‘ of staple food before Eid prayer, not simply one meal. Follow qualified local guidance on quantity and monetary payment.

fastingRules.title: What Invalidates the Fast
rules: Sexual intercourse during the fasting hours
Intentional vomiting (ask a scholar about details)
Onset of menstruation or postnatal bleeding

fastingRules.title: What Does NOT Invalidate the Fast
rules: Forgetful eating or drinking: the hadith directs the person to continue fasting (Bukhari 1933); ask your scholar about school-specific make-up rules
Brushing teeth (being careful not to swallow)
Taking a shower, while avoiding swallowing water
fastingRules.note: This is not an exhaustive list. Medical procedures, injections, inhalers and accidental swallowing require specific guidance; scholars differ on some treatments. Never withhold necessary medicine based on this app.

fastingRules.title: Who is Exempt from Fasting
rules: Those whose illness makes fasting harmful or unduly difficult
Pregnant or breastfeeding women who cannot fast or reasonably fear harm
Women during menstruation or postnatal bleeding (they do not fast during this time)
fastingRules.note: Children are not required to make up pre-puberty fasts. Missed fasts due to temporary illness, travel, menstruation or postnatal bleeding are generally made up later. Permanent inability and pregnancy/nursing can involve different fidya and make-up rules across Sunni schools; consult a qualified scholar.

healthBenefits.title: Metabolic Health
healthBenefits.description: Some time-restricted eating studies report improved blood glucose control. These findings do not establish that Ramadan dry fasting is safe or beneficial for everyone, particularly people using diabetes medicines.
healthBenefits.source: NIDDK: intermittent fasting and type 2 diabetes

healthBenefits.title: Weight Management
healthBenefits.description: Time-restricted eating may help some adults manage weight, but it is not a guarantee of weight loss or a reason to fast when unsafe. Ramadan fasting differs from research protocols that permit water.
healthBenefits.source: NIDDK: intermittent fasting and type 2 diabetes

healthBenefits.title: Safety Comes First
healthBenefits.description: Fasting can pose risks including low blood glucose and dehydration. Discuss your circumstances and medicines with your healthcare team before fasting; do not adjust medicines based on this app.
